question: What did Indian private capital do in 2023, and what are the financial institutions doing with the pool they run on?
answer: Activity fell to 2018 levels with the decline concentrated in repriced technology, and in credit it is governance rather than availability that decides how far a generative-AI programme reaches.
$comment: Written when this deck was cut from seven unrelated subjects to two. A first reader rated the sampler 3-4/10 and its first finding was that the titles did not add up; the cover named one document, the footer another, and two dividers promised sections a third of the pages contradicted. Every claim here is checked against the exhibit it sits on - three of them were wrong before this file existed.

pages.claim: PE-VC activity declined by ~36% in 2023, to $39bn: 2018 levels, not 2019

settles.what: annual PE-VC investment in India, $B, 2013 to 2023, against the 2018 and 2019 marks

pages.adds: Two slow deployment years have aged the 2021 vintage, so the pressure to deploy arrives before the pressure to reprice

pages.claim: Traditional sectors demonstrated resilience in an otherwise slowing market

settles.what: investment split across traditional, software and new-age technology, 2021 to 2023, $B

pages.adds: The mix is back where it sat before the 2021 cycle, so this is a reversion rather than a rotation into something new

pages.claim: Sector outlook: healthcare and manufacturing stay strong while IT stays soft

settles.what: 2023 deal value, year-on-year change and outlook across seven sectors

pages.adds: The three sectors with a positive outlook are the three backed by policy or demographics rather than by funding conditions

pages.claim: Four conditions decide whether the 2024 recovery holds

settles.what: each condition, what 2023 showed, and what has to be true in 2024

pages.adds: Three of the four are testable by mid-year, so the recovery case can be checked rather than waited out

pages.claim: Investment themes: a return to fundamentals across sectors and geographies

settles.what: the six themes, each against its 2023 value and direction

pages.adds: Every theme here is a consequence of the same repricing, which is why they are read together rather than picked from

pages.claim: Retail and corporate banking hold two thirds of the revenue pool, mostly domestic

settles.what: the 2025 banking revenue pool by business line and geography, $B

pages.adds: Two thirds of the pool is domestic retail and corporate, so a domestic rate move matters more to the plan than any international build

pages.claim: Institutions prioritise productivity improvement when initiating GenAI use cases

settles.what: how 33 credit institutions ranked four initiating factors first

pages.adds: Return on investment ranks last, so these programmes are being justified on capacity rather than on a business case

pages.claim: Most institutions have access to external GenAI tools but half require internal guidelines first

settles.what: how 33 institutions grant access: to named teams, to almost all colleagues, or not at all

pages.adds: Governance, not availability, is what decides how far a deployment reaches inside an institution

pages.claim: Most institutions are testing GenAI use cases, with super regionals leading deployment

settles.what: use cases by institution type across five development stages

pages.adds: Nothing has been discontinued anywhere, which means nobody has yet met a case they were willing to stop paying for
